identity.title: A Keplerian disk around a Class 0 source: ALMA observations of VLA1623A

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper, we present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) Early Science Cycle 0 observations of VLA1623A in 1.3 mm continuum and C$^{18}$O emission.

evidence.quote: located in $\rho$ Ophiuchus ($d \sim$ 120pc, (cite: loinard2008))
located in $\rho$ Ophiuchus ($d \sim$ 120pc, (cite: loinard2008))

question.value: Is the C18O emission around the Class 0 source VLA1623A tracing a rotationally supported (Keplerian) disk rather than a pseudo-disk/infall structure?

evidence.quote: In order to determine whether the C$^{18}$O emission is tracing a rotationally supported disk about VLA1623A, we perform Position-Velocity diagram analysis and models of the C$^{18}$O emission
ADS/JAO.ALMA# 2011.0.00902.S which was obtained by N.M.M. while was a Master student at National Tsing Hua University
Observations were done in Band 6 (230 GHz) using the extended configuration

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four lines DCO+ (3-2), C18O (2-1), N2D+ (3-2), 12CO (2-1) plus continuum

evidence.quote: The spectral configuration was set-up to observe four molecular lines: DCO$^{+}$ (3-2), C$^{18}$O (2-1), N$_{2}$D$^{+}$ (3-2) and $^{12}$CO (2-1), in addition to continuum.
In this paper we will only analyse and discuss the results of C$^{18}$O and continuum.

evidence.quote: consisting of 16 antennae with a maximum baseline of $\sim$400m
The synthesized beam size is 0.79$\ensuremath{''}$ $\times$ 0.54$\ensuremath{''}$ for continuum and 0.79$\ensuremath{''}$ $\times$ 0.61$\ensuremath{''}$ for C$^{18}$O

evidence.quote: our ALMA observations have higher sensitivity (rms noise = 18 mJy beam$^{-1}$) and velocity resolution (0.0833 km s$^{-1}$)

To calculate the time since collapse for $R_{\rm c}$ = 150 AU, we use the equation from (cite: belloche2013)

analysis_steps.goal: Measure continuum fluxes and compare with SMA

method.value: Integrated continuum emission over source-sized region to 3 sigma; imstat comparison with SMA for VLA1623B

evidence.quote: Integrated fluxes for each source were obtained by integrating the continuum emission over a region the size of the source out to 3$\sigma$.

validation.value: ALMA VLA1623B 96.3 mJy vs SMA 96.8 mJy consistent

evidence.quote: for the ALMA data, VLA1623B has an integrated flux of 96.3$\pm$0.7 mJy. This shows that both observations are consistent.

method.value: PV diagram along major axis (PA 35 deg); UV-space peak positions per channel rotated, fit with power law v=aR^n in log-log; red-shifted points v>5.0 km/s only

evidence.quote: The data points are fit with a power law of the form $v = aR^{n}$ and we find that the UV-space PV diagram is independent of the inclination angle of the structure.
which uses the mean $v_{\rm lsr}$, 3.7 km s$^{-1}$.

fitting.value: power law fit in log-log space

evidence.quote: projected onto Position-Velocity space and fit with a power law in log-log space

validation.value: fits for any vlsr within error

evidence.quote: The results of the fit for any $v_{\rm lsr}$ are within the error of the fit presented here

analysis_steps.goal: Thin disk kinematic modelling of five cases with foreground absorption

method.value: Analytical thin-disk model (no radiative transfer) with free fall, free fall+Keplerian, conserved AM, infall+Keplerian, Keplerian velocity fields; three Gaussian absorbing layers; compared via channel-map residuals

evidence.quote: we proceed to further investigate the structure and its kinematics using an analytical thin disk model with the addition of absorbing foreground material.

key_parameters.value: M*=0.2 Msun, PA=35 deg, vlsr=4.0 km/s fixed; free: vwidth 0.1-1.0 km/s, i 0-90 deg, Rout 100-200 AU

evidence.quote: The attempted value ranges for each parameter are: 0.1 km s$^{-1}$ $\leq$ $v_{\rm width}$ $\leq$ 1.0 km s$^{-1}$

assumptions.value: d=120 pc; optically thin emission, constant density, adjusted temperature gradient

evidence.quote: we assume the observed emission is optically thin, and set the density as a constant and adjust the temperature gradient to match the observed spectral profile.

fitting.value: manual adjustment by eye then residuals; least residual deemed best

evidence.quote: We deemed the model with the least residual the best fit (discarding the filaments to the north and south).
Appendix [8](#seccomp) shows the channel map for each model, compared with observations and the corresponding residual.

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate time since collapse for 150 AU disk

method.value: Belloche (2013) Rc equation with Omega=4e-14 rad/s, a=0.2 km/s

evidence.quote: we obtain $t$ = 8.5 $\times$ 10$^{5}$ yr for a centrifugal radius of 150 AU.
We use the same region and task (CASA’s imstat task) to measure the integrated flux for both datasets.

findings_qualitative.value: Filament-like C18O features north and south of the disk, possibly disk wind or outflow-entrained material

evidence.quote: the high sensitivity allowed the detection of previously unknown filament-like features, located to the north and south of VLA1623A’s C$^{18}$O disk structure

claims.hypothesis: Class 0 source VLA1623A hosts a rotationally supported Keplerian disk
claims.experiment: PV diagrams and thin-disk models of ALMA C18O (2-1)
claims.result: v ∝ R^-0.5±0.08 for high velocities; Keplerian or infall+Keplerian with Rcrit=150 AU fit best; M*=0.22 Msun
claims.finding: Emission traces a Keplerian disk out to 150 AU

evidence.quote: we determine that the emission is tracing a Keplerian disk out to 150 AU around a 0.2$\pm$0.02 M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ protostar.

claims.hypothesis: Free fall or conserved angular momentum explain the structure
claims.experiment: Modelled these cases and compared residuals
claims.result: Free fall gives gradient along outflow; conserved AM mismatches blue peak

evidence.quote: Thus we determine that this scenario does not match the observations.

claims.hypothesis: Weak, misaligned magnetic fields favour early disk formation
claims.experiment: Comparison with literature polarization and models
claims.result: Field misaligned by 84 deg and weak
claims.finding: Consistent with Krumholz et al. predictions

evidence.quote: The presence of a fairly large rotationally supported disk around VLA1623A is consistent with (cite: krumholz2013)’s predictions

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Free fall, free fall+Keplerian (small Rcrit), conserved AM models rejected

evidence.quote: It is clear that the pure free fall case does not fit the observed C$^{18}$O emission

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot distinguish infall+Keplerian from pure Keplerian in outer 30 AU due to low S/N; foreground absorption

evidence.quote: This uncertainty is due to the low S/N ratio (5$\sigma$) in the outer edges of the observed disk structure

referee_caveats_inferred: Model fits by eye without formal chi-square or uncertainties
Optically thin assumption questionable given large opacities

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA project 2011.0.00902.S named; public status not explicitly stated
